=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:324-339 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In decide(), the time window restarts after a governor escalation (`start = index + 1`), but `items = rounds(ordered, current_approach(ordered))` still counts every round from before the escalation. glm also flags that `approaches(ordered)` / `can_replan` is not reset either.
  WHY: An issue escalated at 5 or more rounds is escalated or re-planned again on the next tick after a person resumes it, as soon as one new round (even `review ok`) is journalled. `trailing_failed` also counts failures from before the escalation. No table case covers a resume with 5 or more prior rounds. Severity disagrees: sonnet and glm say MAJOR, minimax says NIT (confidence 2), gemini gives none; the highest is used.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:339 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The max_rounds cap now fires on the round count alone (`if len(items) >= limits["max_rounds"] and MERGING_LABEL not in _labels(labels)`), with no requirement that the newest round failed. Every autofix commit is journalled as a `review ok` round (scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:707).
  WHY: A PR whose rounds all pass reaches PERSIST_MAX_ROUNDS=5 after the implement round plus 4 autofix commits, which is inside review_autofix's default of 5 iterations (.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3132). With `ai:done` on the issue, decide() returns `escalate open_pr:max_rounds` (sonnet), or pulls a healthy PR back to planning (gemini).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22877-23119 (standalone hook; persist_budget_govern_issue `length < 100` check ~19629; managed hook ~30737-30739) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `_standalone_staged_support_cache_available="complete"` (the full comment history is already fetched), the governor's `jq -e 'type == "array" and length < 100'` check still fails for issues with 100 or more comments.
  WHY: Each such issue gets one extra paginated comments read per tick, a duplicate API read that the cache was meant to prevent (§14).
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py:Test suite failure | severity=unspecified | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR changes .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs/INVENTORY.md, which are outside the issue's file grant.
  WHY: The pre-push gate lists this as a change-caused failure, which blocks the production release.
- tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py:Test suite failure | severity=unspecified | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR breaks the poller's integration tests, which suggests the new persist_budget integration violates orchestration contracts.
  WHY: This failure blocks the production release.
- tests/test_persist_postmerge_verify.py:test_phase_labels_mirror_label_helpers_and_label_is_registered | severity=unspecified | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR breaks the phase label registration contract.
  WHY: An incorrect label sync blocks the orchestrator's state machine and prevents correct issue tracking.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:Test suite failure | severity=unspecified | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR breaks the security guards for GitHub API writes (e.g. `test_dispatchable_workflows_match_the_gh_workflow_run_allow_rules`).
  WHY: The guard rejects API writes that are not gated properly, which blocks the production release.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19728 | severity=unspecified | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: When the escalation comment fails to post, the code sends a Telegram WARNING, but the label edit has already been committed.
  WHY: The issue ends up labelled `ai:needs-human` with no explanation for the user, and the governor logs `error` instead of `blocked` for that action.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:325-333 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The elapsed-time window starts after the newest `governor` escalation instead of at the journal's first entry, which contradicts P6's "Elapsed since the first entry" rule.
  WHY: After a resume, PERSIST_MAX_HOURS is measured from the resumed work, so repeated escalation and resumption can keep work active beyond the configured time cap.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:~95-97 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The module-level constants `ACTIONS` and `IGNORE_LABELS` are defined but never used. The shell case list and the `ignored()` helper duplicate their values inline.
  WHY: This dead code can drift from the real allowlist, so the two implementations could start to disagree.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~30760-30762 (and standalone hook ~23116-23118) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `jq ... > "${STATE_FILE}.persist_budget.tmp" 2>/dev/null && mv ...` can replace the state file with the literal `null` when jq exits 0 on empty or malformed input.
  WHY: This rare case (STATE_FILE emptied by an earlier crash) silently corrupts orchestrator state, and later stall/wave recovery then fails.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:~326-330 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `start = index + 1` loop followed by `ordered[start]` can raise IndexError if the early return for `newest_governor and outcome == "blocked"` is ever removed.
  WHY: This is defence in depth only, because the current early return makes the path safe.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~23111-23113 vs ~30747 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Only the managed call to `persist_budget_govern_issue` redirects `< /dev/null`; the standalone call does not.
  WHY: This is a hygiene inconsistency with no bug today, because the function does not read stdin.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:~75-79 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `try: import attempt_journal except Exception: attempt_journal = None` swallows an import failure silently.
  WHY: The governor then returns `journal_absent` for every issue and becomes a repo-wide no-op, with no log line showing the cause.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Scope: ... Stay within the granted files..." / "Stay inside the files the plan lists for P6." (issue #8561)
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/ci.yml, docs/INVENTORY.md (or the `files_touched` grant in issue #8561)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Several reviewers say the same thing. The PR diff changes .github/workflows/ci.yml (line 672) and docs/INVENTORY.md (line 190), neither of which is in the grant. The pre-push gate attributes the `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py` failure to this in two consecutive runs. The edits are needed by `test_ci_wires_every_test_file` / `inventory_parity`, but the grant was never widened, and the implementation PR cannot modify it.
- requirement: "The PR body uses `Refs` (never an auto-close keyword) for the orchestrator tracking issue."
  expected_change_site: PR description (auto-generated)
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The PR description contains "Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/8561". If #8561 is an `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issue, this violates §19/§21.
- requirement: "The P6 deliverables and tests listed in the plan are implemented and pass" / pre-push gate change-caused failures on head 46b9af4
  expected_change_site: the PR head (46b9af4) test gate / the implementation files the gate attributes
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The gate reports `ruff`, `shellcheck`, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py and tests/test_persist_postmerge_verify.py::test_phase_labels_mirror_label_helpers_and_label_is_registered as change-caused, but none of them traces to a hunk in the diff. The newest gate ended `container_rc_137` (OOM) with 0 tests run, and the editor's local runs were partial, so acceptance is not demonstrated.
- requirement: When rounds reach `PERSIST_MAX_ROUNDS`, the governor should "re-plan if approaches are below `PERSIST_MAX_APPROACHES`, else escalate."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/persist_budget.py`, `decide()`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: For an open-PR label, lines 358–361 return `escalate open_pr:<trigger>` even when approaches are below the cap. Table case `max_rounds_review_cycling_with_open_pr_escalates` asserts this deviation, and the plan does not authorise it.
- requirement: P6 "API: at most 2 writes per decision" (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md:497)
  expected_change_site: `persist_budget_govern_issue` in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Two reviewers give the write counts. An escalation does a label edit (line 19724), a comment (line 19731) and a journal append (lines 19743–19746). A standalone re-plan also writes state (lines 23124–23125). A re-plan does up to 4 writes: label edit, `/answer` comment, journal append and state write. glm notes this is a known deviation documented in agents.d/8427-p6-persist-budget.md that was declined earlier.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:decide() (`items = rounds(ordered, current_approach(ordered))`, time-window loop `start = index + 1`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The time window restarts after a governor escalation, but `items` still holds the rounds from before the escalation. The last run also dropped `failed(items[-1])` from max_rounds, so a resumed `open_pr:max_rounds` / `max_approaches:max_rounds` issue is escalated again after one new round. The same applies to `failed_rounds` via `trailing_failed`.
  WHY: A journal of plan, 5 review-ok rounds, governor blocked, then 1 review ok gives `len(items)`=6≥5, so decide() returns `escalate open_pr:max_rounds` again. No table case covers this. Fix: `items = rounds(ordered[start:], current_approach(ordered))` plus a table case.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:OPEN_PR_LABELS / count-only max_rounds trigger / `open_pr:{trigger}` escalate (interacts with scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:707, .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3132) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Every autofix commit is journalled as `review ok`, so a PR with no failures reaches PERSIST_MAX_ROUNDS=5 within review_autofix's default of 5 iterations and is escalated `open_pr:max_rounds` while it carries `ai:done`.
  WHY: On an idle tick between autofix iterations, the governor adds `ai:needs-human` and posts "Persistence budget reached" on a PR whose rounds all passed. Fix: count only failed rounds while a PR is open, or exempt `ai:done`/`ai:implementing`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:standalone hook `_pb_standalone_comments="${comments_json}"` (cache `complete` set at line 22877) / `jq -e 'type == "array" and length < 100'` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the cache state is `complete`, an issue with 100 or more comments still triggers a second paginated comments read in the governor.
  WHY: One extra paginated read per such issue per tick. Fix: pass a flag that skips the length check.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
